I'm not giving presentation to the company, just a short presentation for those that aren't familiar with the bitcoin. evidence.quote: There are not too many scams, hypes in Skype, which are usually to collect data, or simply copy bitcoin codes and something like that

textual.context: Presented as a general cautionary discussion while explaining Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies; the statement is not explicitly attributed to OneCoin.
textual.potential_relevance: The source describes a concrete data or cryptocurrency-code collection mechanism associated with Skype scams, which may require later assessment of whether the video connects that mechanism to any promoted company or destination.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish that any data was collected, that any Bitcoin code was copied, or that OneCoin used this mechanism. The ASR wording may contain transcription errors.

visual.context: Visible context is a commercial-looking banner ad displayed above a CoinMarketCap cryptocurrency market-capitalization table; promotion versus informational discussion is visually a promotion.
visual.potential_relevance: The observed relationship is a Bitcoin-mining offer tied to an action button and a stated payment/entry price of $9.95, which conditionally merits review as a reward/asset-generation claim connected to payment or signup flow.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not show any click, landing page, checkout, account creation, mining terms, actual payout, operator identity verification, or whether the offer was fulfilled.

The discussion of Skype data or Bitcoin-code collection is cautionary and does not establish that OneCoin or the displayed mining advertiser used that mechanism.

This grounds a paid-mining mechanism, although the supplied evidence does not show recurring mining income, payout terms, purchase completion, or fulfillment.
